note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every venue below is described from one source, Portland Parks & Recreation's pickleball page, plus the Census geocode of the address it prints. Where the department is silent, these pages say so: no venue here has stated lighting or parking information, because the department publishes neither for any of them. Where a page reads a location out of an address, it is reading Portland's own street grid, which names the sextant (N, NE, NW, SE, SW) in the address itself.

slots.description: Columbia Park holds eight pickleball courts, equal-largest in Portland for year-round play, and it is one of four sites the parks department names as sanctioned pickleball parks. Portland stripes pickleball only where courts sit roughly 300 to 600 feet from housing, and it names Columbia, Pier, Sellwood and Gabriel as the parks that meet that condition. The courts are described by the city as hard courts with permanent lines, and they are free.
slots.getting_there: 4503 N Lombard St, Portland, OR 97203, in North Portland. The Census geocoder places it in Multnomah County. Lombard is a major east-west arterial across the north of the city. Portland Parks & Recreation publishes no parking information for this site: no lot, no capacity, no permit district. Columbia is a large park with other draws than pickleball, so a busy weekend is a reasonable thing to plan for.
slots.what_to_expect: Eight free courts, first-come and first-served, open dawn to dusk, and bring your own net. The department asks players to limit a session to an hour when others are waiting, and its rules say a single player may not hold a court while a partner is on the way. Restrooms and drinking water are listed. Lighting is not mentioned, here or anywhere else on the city's pickleball page.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Columbia Park have?
faqs.a: Eight, stated by Portland Parks & Recreation as "8 Outdoor hard courts". That ties Columbia with Sellwood Park as the largest year-round pickleball site in the city. Only the Portland Tennis Center has more, and its courts take pickleball for part of the year.

faqs.q: Do I need to bring a net?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's entry ends "bring your own net". Nets are included at only two Portland park sites, Laurelhurst and Gabriel, and this is not one of them.

faqs.q: What are the posted rules on the court?
faqs.a: Games are to eleven, win by two. Play is limited to an hour if others are waiting, and a single player may not hold a court until a partner arrives. Water only: no food, gum, other drinks or glass on the courts. Nothing that marks the surface, and bags and bottles kept off the court. Skateboards, scooters, bicycles, rollerblades and smoking or vaping are prohibited. Wait outside the fence for the players ahead of you to finish.

slots.description: Pier Park has four pickleball courts, and it is the one outdoor site in Portland where the city names the material: "concrete". Everywhere else the department writes "hard courts", which sorts a court into a category without naming a material, so those venues carry no surface. Pier Park is also one of the four parks Portland names as sanctioned pickleball sites, under its rule that striping goes only where courts stand roughly 300 to 600 feet from homes.
slots.getting_there: 10325 N Lombard St, Portland, OR 97203, the same street as Columbia Park and a shade under three miles further north-west along it, out towards St. Johns. The Census geocoder matched the address to Multnomah County. As at every other venue on this site, the parks department publishes nothing at all about parking here, so we have nothing on record to tell you about it.
slots.what_to_expect: Four free courts on concrete, with permanent lines, open dawn to dusk on a first-come basis, and bring your own net. Four courts is a small site by the standards of Columbia and Sellwood, so the department's one-hour courtesy limit is more likely to matter on a busy afternoon. The amenities line lists restrooms and, unlike the other outdoor parks, does not mention drinking water. That is an absence in the city's list rather than a statement that there is none. Lighting is not mentioned.

faqs.q: What surface are Pier Park's courts?
faqs.a: Concrete. Portland Parks & Recreation writes "4 Outdoor concrete courts", and that is a material rather than a category, so it is published. It makes Pier Park one of only three Portland venues in this directory with a stated surface, and the other two are the wood floors at Southwest and St. Johns community centres.

faqs.q: Is there drinking water?
faqs.a: The city does not say. Its amenities line for Pier Park reads "Amenities: restrooms", where the other outdoor parks say "restrooms and water". Restrooms are recorded and water is left unstated rather than reading a silence as a no.

faqs.q: How far is it from Columbia Park?
faqs.a: About 2.9 miles along North Lombard Street, which the two share. St. Johns Community Center and its two indoor courts sit between them, a little under a mile from Pier. That makes this stretch of North Portland the densest pickleball corridor in the city: twelve free outdoor courts and an indoor room inside three miles of one road.

slots.description: Sellwood Park has eight pickleball courts, tying it with Columbia Park as the largest year-round pickleball site in Portland. It is the third of the four parks the city names as sanctioned pickleball locations. The courts are described as hard courts with permanent lines and are free to play. It is the only eight-court site on the south-east side of the river, and the next largest anywhere in the inner south-east is Laurelhurst's two.
slots.getting_there: 7987 SE Grand Ave, Portland, OR 97202, in the south-east sextant, at the southern end of the city's east side. The Census geocoder matched the address and placed it in Multnomah County. Portland Parks & Recreation publishes no parking guidance for the site: no lot, no street-parking note, no permit district.
slots.what_to_expect: Eight free courts, dawn to dusk, first come first served, and bring your own net. The city's courtesy rules apply: an hour when others are waiting, no holding a court for an absent partner, and games to eleven, win by two. Restrooms and drinking water are listed. Lighting is not stated anywhere on the department's pickleball page, and dusk is the operative limit because the courts are open dawn to dusk rather than to a clock time.

faqs.q: Do I need to book?
faqs.a: No, and you cannot. Portland's outdoor courts are first-come, first-served; the department's rules say no reservations are taken. It also asks that you limit play to an hour when people are waiting.

faqs.q: Why is the surface not listed?
faqs.a: Because the city calls them "hard courts", which names a category rather than a material: asphalt, concrete and acrylic are all hard. The field reads "not stated" for that reason. Pier Park, which says "concrete", is the exception in this city.

faqs.q: What else is nearby on the east side?
faqs.a: Not much. Laurelhurst Park's two dedicated courts are about four miles north, and the Portland Tennis Center is further north again and seasonal. For an eight-court site anywhere south-east of the river, this is the only option.

slots.description: Two courts, and both of them exist only for pickleball. Laurelhurst Park is one of three Portland sites the city describes as 'pickleball only' (the others are Gabriel Park and Hillside Park) and one of only two where nets are included. Across the six free park sites in this city, twenty-one of the twenty-nine courts require you to bring your own net; Laurelhurst is part of the small remainder where a paddle and a ball are the whole kit list. The courts are described as hard courts with permanent lines, and they are free.
slots.getting_there: 3789 SE Oak St, Portland, OR 97214, in the inner south-east, matched by the Census geocoder to Multnomah County. Oak Street is a residential east-side street rather than an arterial. Portland Parks & Recreation publishes no parking information for this venue, as it publishes none for any of the eleven.
slots.what_to_expect: Two courts, free, nets included, permanent lines, dawn to dusk, first come first served. Two courts is the second-smallest pickleball site in the city, so the department's request to limit play to an hour when others are waiting is likely to matter on a good evening. Restrooms and drinking water are listed. Lighting is not stated. Laurelhurst is not one of the four parks Portland names as its sanctioned pickleball sites (Columbia, Pier, Sellwood and Gabriel), which does not make it less official.

faqs.q: Are nets provided at Laurelhurst?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's entry reads "nets included", one of only two Portland park sites where it does; Gabriel Park is the other. At Columbia, Pier, Sellwood and Hillside you are told to bring your own.

faqs.q: What does 'pickleball only' mean here?
faqs.a: That the courts are not shared with tennis or anything else. Portland's rules say pickleball play is permitted only on pickleball courts, and that painting, taping or chalking your own lines on one of the department's tennis courts is not allowed.

faqs.q: What is the nearest bigger site?
faqs.a: Sellwood Park, with eight courts, about four miles south. The Portland Tennis Center is closer at roughly a mile and a half, but its sixteen courts are open to pickleball only from mid June to early September and only through registration.

slots.description: Gabriel Park is the best-equipped free pickleball site in Portland on the evidence the city publishes: six courts, described as 'pickleball only', with permanent lines and nets included, at no cost. It is the only venue in the city that is both a named sanctioned pickleball park and a dedicated, nets-included site. Columbia, Pier and Sellwood are sanctioned but you bring your own net; Laurelhurst and Hillside are dedicated but smaller.
slots.getting_there: 4508 SW Nevada St, Portland, OR 97219, in the south-west sextant, one of three venues in this set on the west side of the river, with Hillside Park and Southwest Community Center. The Census geocoder matched the address to Multnomah County. Southwest Community Center, the city's largest indoor site, is about 250 metres away, one of the closest pairings of an outdoor and an indoor pickleball venue anywhere in this directory. No parking information is published by the parks department, and Gabriel is a large multi-use park.
slots.what_to_expect: Six free courts with nets already provided, dawn to dusk, first come first served. Six is enough that the one-hour courtesy limit is less likely to bite than at Laurelhurst or Hillside, and the dedicated striping means you are not negotiating with tennis players for the space. Restrooms and drinking water are listed. Lighting is not stated, here or at any Portland venue.

faqs.q: What makes it a 'sanctioned' park?
faqs.a: Portland Parks & Recreation names four parks (Columbia, Pier, Sellwood and Gabriel) as the places it has sanctioned pickleball, under a policy of striping only where courts are roughly 300 to 600 feet from housing so that noise carries less.

faqs.q: What else is within reach?
faqs.a: Southwest Community Center, about 250 metres away, with five indoor courts on a wood floor at $6 for adults and $5 for seniors. One address for a dry morning, another for the rest of the year.

faqs.q: Will I get a court?
faqs.a: Unknown. Portland publishes no information about how busy any of its pickleball sites get. Six courts is the second-largest year-round site in the city, nets are already up, and the city's rules ask players to limit a session to an hour when others are waiting and forbid holding a court for a partner who has not arrived.

slots.description: One court. Hillside Park is one of the smallest pickleball venues in this directory, and it is here for the same reason the eight-court sites are: the city states it. The single court is described as 'pickleball only', like the courts at Laurelhurst and Gabriel, and it is free. It is the only outdoor entry on Portland's pickleball page with no amenities line at all. Where the other five parks list restrooms, and four of them water, Hillside's entry ends after "bring your own net". That silence is recorded as not stated rather than as an absence.
slots.getting_there: 653 NW Culpepper Terrace, Portland, OR 97210, in the north-west sextant, up in the west hills. The Census geocoder matched the address to Multnomah County. Culpepper Terrace is a hillside residential street, and the parks department publishes no parking guidance here. A single-court site on a hill street is not somewhere to arrive with a group and no fallback.
slots.what_to_expect: One free court, dedicated to pickleball, with your own net required, dawn to dusk, first come first served. With one court, Portland's rule about limiting play to an hour when others are waiting is the whole etiquette of the place, along with its rule that a single player may not hold a court while a partner is on the way. No restrooms are listed. No water is listed. No lighting is stated.

faqs.q: Is there really only one court?
faqs.a: Yes. Portland Parks & Recreation writes "1 outdoor 'pickleball only' hard court", in the singular. It is one of the smallest venues in this directory, and it is published for the same reason as every other: the operator stated it.

faqs.q: Where is the nearest bigger site?
faqs.a: Gabriel Park, also on the west side, about 3.8 miles south, with six dedicated courts and nets included. If the single court here is taken, that is the nearest real alternative.

faqs.q: Why publish a one-court venue at all?
faqs.a: Because the operator stated it, which is the only test this directory applies. A single court in the west hills is useful for someone who lives near it to be able to find. It is listed with the same three sourced facts as everywhere else (count, address, cost) and the same honest blanks for lighting, parking and amenities.

slots.description: Four indoor courts, and one of the four Portland community centres that take drop-in pickleball players at $6 for adults and $5 for seniors. It is the second-largest indoor site in the city after Southwest Community Center's five. In a city whose outdoor courts run dawn to dusk on surfaces the parks department warns are slippery when wet, the fourteen indoor courts across these four centres are what makes the sport a year-round proposition.
slots.getting_there: 740 SE 106th Ave, Portland, OR 97216, in the south-east sextant well out towards the city's eastern edge, matched by the Census geocoder to Multnomah County. It is the easternmost venue in this set. As at all eleven Portland venues, the parks department publishes nothing about parking.
slots.what_to_expect: Four courts indoors and a published price: $6 for adults, $5 for seniors, per drop-in session, which is the first cost figure any operator in this directory has stated in five cities of trying. What the city does not publish on its pickleball page is the schedule: it lists the count and the price and then directs drop-in players to the community centre's own page for times. Check the centre before travelling. The surface is not stated, unlike the wood floors at Southwest and St. Johns. Neither is whether nets are provided.

faqs.q: When is drop-in pickleball on?
faqs.a: The city does not say on its pickleball page. It points drop-in players to the community centre's own page for schedule details, and that page is not stated here. Settle the timetable before you travel.

faqs.q: Are nets provided?
faqs.a: Not stated. The city says nothing either way for this centre. Two of the four centres do mention nets, but only when describing their registered programmes rather than drop-in play.

faqs.q: What is the nearest outdoor pickleball?
faqs.a: Nothing close. The city lists no outdoor pickleball site in outer east Portland. The six free parks are in the north, the south-east, the inner east and the west. For anyone in this part of the city, these four indoor courts are the option.

slots.description: Five indoor courts on a wood floor: the largest indoor pickleball site in Portland and one of only three venues in this city with a published surface. It appears twice on the city's pickleball page, once under indoor courts with a count and a drop-in price, and again under registered activities as "Indoor wood courts, permanent lines, nets provided". From that second listing the wood floor and the restrooms are recorded, because they belong to the building. The nets are not, because they describe what a registered programme puts out.
slots.getting_there: 6820 SW 45th Ave, Portland, OR 97219, in the south-west sextant, matched by the Census geocoder to Multnomah County. It is about 250 metres from Gabriel Park's six dedicated courts, near enough to walk between them, which makes this corner of south-west Portland the one part of the city where a large free outdoor site and the largest indoor site sit within easy reach of each other. No parking information is published.
slots.what_to_expect: Five courts indoors, wood floor, permanent lines, $6 for adults and $5 for seniors as a drop-in. There is also a registered pickleball programme here, booked through an ActiveNet account, which the city says takes no court reservations. The schedule for either is on the centre's own page rather than the city's pickleball page, so check before you travel. Restrooms and drinking water are listed. Whether nets are out for drop-in play is not something the city states.

faqs.q: Why does it say nets are not stated when the page says 'nets provided'?
faqs.a: Because that phrase appears only in the description of the centre's registered programme, not of drop-in play. It is very likely the same nets go up for both, but very likely is not a source, so the field stays empty.

faqs.q: Do I have to register?
faqs.a: Not for drop-in play, which is what the five-court figure and the $6 adult and $5 senior price describe; you pay at the door. The registered pickleball programme does require an ActiveNet account and pre-registration, and the city adds that no court reservations are taken, so registering signs you up for the programme rather than for a slot on a particular court.

slots.description: Two indoor courts on a wood floor, the smallest of Portland's four drop-in community centres, at the same $6 adult and $5 senior rate as the others. Like Southwest Community Center it is listed twice on the city's pickleball page: once with its court count and price, once under registered activities as "Indoor wood courts, permanent lines, nets provided". The wood floor and the restrooms are properties of the building and are recorded. The nets describe a programme and are not.
slots.getting_there: 8427 N Central St, Portland, OR 97203, in the north sextant, matched by the Census geocoder to Multnomah County. It shares its postcode with Columbia Park and Pier Park and sits between the two of them, which puts twelve free outdoor courts and an indoor room within a short distance of each other. Nothing about parking is published.
slots.what_to_expect: Two courts, wood floor, permanent lines, drop-in at $6 for adults and $5 for seniors, plus a registered programme booked through ActiveNet that takes no court reservations. Two courts is small enough that the schedule matters more than the count, and the schedule is on the centre's own page rather than the city's pickleball page. Restrooms and drinking water are listed. Nets for drop-in play are not stated.

faqs.q: What else is nearby?
faqs.a: Columbia Park and Pier Park are both on North Lombard Street in the same postcode, with eight and four free outdoor courts respectively. If the weather is dry, they are a much larger option a short distance away.

faqs.q: What does drop-in cost?
faqs.a: $6 for adults and $5 for seniors, the same as at all four Portland community centres. This venue's line is worded slightly differently on the city's page ("$6/Adult and $5 for seniors") but the figures are identical.

faqs.q: How does drop-in differ from the registered programme?
faqs.a: Drop-in is paid at the door, and the court count here refers to it. The registered programme is booked through an ActiveNet account in advance and takes no court reservations. It is the registered programme's entry that describes the wood floor and permanent lines.

slots.description: Three indoor courts at the standard Portland drop-in rate of $6 for adults and $5 for seniors. Montavilla is the plainest entry of the four community centres on the city's pickleball page: a name, an address, a court count and a price, with no second listing under registered activities and so no statement about the floor, the nets or the amenities. It is the indoor venue about which the least is known, and the record reflects that rather than borrowing detail from the centres that say more.
slots.getting_there: 8219 NE Glisan St, Portland, OR 97220, in the north-east sextant on an east-west arterial, matched by the Census geocoder to Multnomah County. It is the only venue in this set in the NE quadrant. The parks department publishes no parking information here, as at every other Portland venue.
slots.what_to_expect: Three courts indoors at $6 adult and $5 senior per drop-in session, with the schedule on the community centre's own page rather than the city's pickleball page. Beyond that, the city has not said: no surface, no note on nets, no amenities line. Three courts is the middle of Portland's indoor range, more than St. Johns, fewer than East Portland and Southwest.

faqs.q: What surface are the courts?
faqs.a: Not stated. Montavilla appears only once on the city's pickleball page, in the drop-in list, which gives a count and a price and nothing else. Southwest and St. Johns are recorded as wood because their second listings say so; there is no equivalent sentence here.

faqs.q: Are there restrooms?
faqs.a: Not stated. The city lists no amenities for this centre. That is a silence in the source, not a statement that there are none.

faqs.q: What is the nearest outdoor pickleball?
faqs.a: Laurelhurst Park, a little over two miles west, with two courts dedicated to pickleball, nets included, free and open dawn to dusk. The Portland Tennis Center is a similar distance and much larger at sixteen courts, but its pickleball runs only from mid June to early September and requires registration.

slots.description: Sixteen outdoor courts, one of the largest single venues in this directory, and the one where the number needs its sentence read to the end. Portland Parks & Recreation states "16 outdoor hard courts, permanent lines, nets provided", and then: "Available from mid June until early September." Pickleball here is a registered summer programme, booked through an ActiveNet account, with no court reservations taken. The courts and their permanent lines are not seasonal; the access to them for pickleball is.
slots.getting_there: 324 NE 12th Ave, Portland, OR 97232, in the north-east sextant just across the river from the city centre, the most central venue in this set, matched by the Census geocoder to Multnomah County. It is about a mile and a half from Laurelhurst Park's two dedicated courts, the nearest year-round alternative on this side of the river. No parking information is published.
slots.what_to_expect: In season, sixteen outdoor hard courts with permanent lines and nets provided, run as mixer activities requiring an ActiveNet account and pre-registration, with no court reservations. Out of season, this is not a pickleball venue. The city does not state a price: registration goes through ActiveNet, which prices per activity, and no figure appears on the pickleball page, so the cost reads "not stated" rather than free. Restrooms and drinking water are listed. Lighting is not mentioned.

faqs.q: Can I play pickleball here in winter?
faqs.a: Not on the evidence the city publishes. Its entry says the courts are "available from mid June until early September" and lists the venue under registered activities requiring pre-registration. For year-round outdoor play in Portland, the six free park sites are the answer; Columbia and Sellwood have eight courts each.

faqs.q: Do I need to book a court?
faqs.a: You need to register, and you cannot book a court. The city says all pickleball activities require an ActiveNet account and pre-registration, and separately that no court reservations are taken here. You sign up for the programme, not for a slot on a particular court.

sources.evidence: One page carrying every venue line quoted above, e.g. "Columbia Park | 4503 N Lombard St., Portland, OR 97203 / 8 Outdoor hard courts, free, permanent lines, bring your own net. Amenities: restrooms and water."; "Hillside Park | 653 NW Culpepper Terrace Portland, OR 97210 / 1 outdoor 'pickleball only' hard court, free, bring your own net."; "Portland Tennis Center | 324 NE 12th Ave., Portland, OR 97232 / 16 outdoor hard courts, permanent lines, nets provided. Available from mid June until early September."; "Southwest Community Center | 6820 SW 45th Ave., Portland, OR 97219 / Indoor wood courts, permanent lines, nets provided." Also the sanctioned-parks sentence ("PP&R has sanctioned pickleball courts at Columbia, Pier, Sellwood, and Gabriel Park"), the 300-to-600-feet striping rule, and the posted court rules.
